name: Lutherie and tonewood selection
open_problem: Selecting a specific piece of tonewood (spruce/maple billet) for a violin and predicting its acoustic outcome is done by expert feel — tapping, flexing, eyeing grain — because the internal structure of wood is uncertain and only roughly one tree in a thousand meets professional criteria. There is no tooling that maps a raw billet's measurable physical properties to the finished instrument's sound, so makers rely on tacit, hard-to-transfer judgment.
verbatim_quote: The craft of luthiers, lutherie, is commonly divided into the two main categories of makers of stringed instruments that are plucked or strummed and makers of stringed instruments that are bowed.

name: Change ringing method composition (campanology)
open_problem: Composing a 'peal' or 'touch' requires arranging thousands of bell-order permutations so that no row repeats ('truth') while remaining musical and physically ringable, and the conductor must memorise the entire composition. This combinatorial design over factorial-sized permutation groups is still done largely by hand and by tradition by a small community of expert conductors/composers.
verbatim_quote: Change ringing is the art of ringing a set of tuned bells in a tightly controlled manner to produce precise variations in their successive striking sequences, known as "changes".

name: Inpainting / retouching in painting conservation
open_problem: Filling losses (lacunae) in a damaged painting so the fill blends with surrounding colours but does not cover any original paint, while staying reversible and ethically distinguishable, is an extremely time-consuming hand process driven by case-by-case expert judgement and contested philosophy. Generative image inpainting exists for photos but is essentially unused for physical conservation decisions, colour-matching aged varnish, or reversibility constraints.
verbatim_quote: Inpainting is the work done by a conservator-restorer to reinstate obliterated or damaged areas in a pictorial layer, in a way that blends with the surrounding colors but without covering any of the original paint.

name: Stained glass conservation and matching antique glass
open_problem: When restoring a historic window, matching replacement glass to the original colour depth, texture, seeds (bubbles) and light behaviour is the most technically demanding and visually critical step; conservators do it by eye, sometimes plating two layers (one for colour, one for texture) so the patch does not read as a patch. There is no computational tool to predict perceived match under varying transmitted light or to recommend a plating recipe.
verbatim_quote: When matching colored textured glass is not available, it is possible to use two layers of glass, one for texture and one for color, rather than installing a poorly matched piece that would be visible.

name: Labanotation / dance notation transcription
open_problem: Transcribing live or recorded human movement into a Labanotation score (direction, level, body part, duration, dynamics) is difficult, time-consuming and depends on a shrinking pool of trained notators; not all expressive movement maps cleanly to symbols. Automatic, accurate motion-to-Labanotation generation remains an open, barely-served problem, leaving most of the world's choreography unrecorded.
verbatim_quote: Labanotation is a system for analyzing and recording human movement, invented by Austro-Hungarian choreographer and dancer Rudolf von Laban (1879–1958).

name: Tuvan throat singing / overtone singing technique
open_problem: Throat singers produce two simultaneous pitches by precisely shaping the vocal tract to focus a single overtone above a sustained drone; mastering and teaching styles like khoomei, sygyt and kargyraa is done by ear and imitation. There is essentially no real-time pedagogical tool that analyses a learner's overtone focusing and gives corrective feedback on tongue/pharynx shaping.
verbatim_quote: Khoomei is traditionally a softer sounding style, with the fundamental (or drone) usually in the low-mid to midrange of the singer's normal voice.

name: Traditional lake pigment making
open_problem: Producing historical lake pigments (e.g. madder, carmine) by precipitating a natural dye onto a mordant is a centuries-old recipe craft whose colour, lightfastness and transparency depend on subtle, poorly-documented control of pH, mordant ratio and source material. Reconstructing or optimising these recipes for conservation/reproduction is done by trial-and-error by a handful of specialists.
verbatim_quote: A lake pigment is a pigment made by precipitating a dye with an inert binder, or mordant, usually a metallic salt.

name: Marionette manipulation (string puppetry)
open_problem: Animating a marionette convincingly through many strings (Burmese yoke thé use 18–19 wires) is a dexterous expert skill, hardest when there is no central control rod; transmission of this craft is endangered. There is little to no tooling for capturing, notating, or assisting marionette manipulation, or for mapping desired character motion to per-string control.
verbatim_quote: Burmese marionettes are very intricate and their use requires dexterous skills, employing 18 or 19 wires for male and female characters respectively, with each puppet controlled by only one puppeteer.

name: Gift economy and obligations of reciprocity
open_problem: In gift economies the obligations to give, receive and reciprocate (Mauss) govern social standing, yet deciding the appropriate counter-gift, timing and value to maintain honour is tacit cultural knowledge. There is no formal/computational modelling tool used by communities to reason about reciprocity obligations, debt of honour, or fairness in gift exchange networks.
verbatim_quote: Because of the bond between giver and gift, the act of giving creates a social bond with an obligation to reciprocate on the part of the recipient.

name: Computus (calculation of the date of Easter)
open_problem: Computus is the traditional algorithmic determination of moveable feast dates from ecclesiastical lunar/solar cycles (golden number, epact, Sunday letter). Reconciling competing historical computistical systems, reconstructing dates in fragmentary medieval calendars, and resolving Julian/Gregorian and Eastern/Western divergences is specialist manual scholarship with little modern tooling beyond fixed formulas.
verbatim_quote: Easter is the Sunday following the Paschal full moon date, which is the ecclesiastical full moon date on or after the ecclesiastical equinox on 21 March.

name: Divination and interpretation of signs/omens
open_problem: Across hundreds of divination systems (haruspicy, augury, scrying, casting lots) the practitioner's core task is interpreting effectively random or natural phenomena into meaningful guidance for a querent within a ritual frame. This interpretive act is purely human/traditional; the under-served angle is formalising and comparing the symbolic interpretation systems themselves, not predicting the future.
verbatim_quote: Divination is the attempt to gain insight into a question or situation by way of a magic ritual or practice.

name: Barter and the double coincidence of wants
open_problem: Pure barter requires a double coincidence of wants — each party must want exactly what the other holds at the same time and place — which is improbable and historically limits moneyless trade. In modern barter rings, swap meets and sharing/gift networks, finding multi-party trade cycles that satisfy everyone is done informally; there is little practical matching tooling for community-scale non-monetary exchange.
verbatim_quote: The coincidence of wants (often known as double coincidence of wants) is an economic phenomenon where two parties each hold an item that the other wants, so they exchange these items directly.

name: Funerary / mortuary customs
open_problem: Mortuary customs (interment, excarnation, heart-burial, grave goods, mourning rites) are a vast, culturally-specific complex of beliefs and practices, much of it undocumented and endangered. Systematically recording, comparing and reconstructing variation in death rituals across cultures (and matching archaeological remains to likely practices) is manual ethnographic/archaeological work.
verbatim_quote: Funerary customs comprise the complex of beliefs and practices used by a culture to remember and respect the dead, from interment, to various monuments, prayers, and rituals undertaken in their honour.

name: Mechanical watch regulation (horology)
open_problem: Regulating a mechanical movement — adjusting the escapement and balance so the watch keeps time across positions, temperatures and states of wind — requires cleaning, lubrication and calibration by a skilled watchmaker working by feel and timegrapher traces. Diagnosing rate errors and prescribing adjustments remains an expert manual craft with little assistive intelligence.
verbatim_quote: Mechanical watches are typically not as accurate as quartz watches, and they eventually require periodic cleaning, lubrication and calibration by a skilled watchmaker.

name: Kinship terminology systems analysis
open_problem: Different cultures encode relatives with structured kin-term systems whose generative logic (how terms compose to compute any relation) is an algebraic structure that anthropologists currently derive largely by hand. Eliciting, formalising and comparing these terminologies across the world's languages is labour-intensive and under-tooled despite being amenable to computation.
verbatim_quote: During the 1950s and '60s, the formal analysis of systems of classification on the basis of their different component distinctions within a semantic domain became known as "componential analysis."

name: Go scoring and life-and-death / seki determination
open_problem: Settling a Go game requires agreeing which groups are alive or dead and resolving ambiguous positions such as seki, where neither player can play without being captured — a judgement amateurs frequently dispute and that traditional scoring leaves to consensus. While top engines play superbly, accessible, explainable tools that adjudicate disputed life-and-death/seki and teach the reasoning to beginners are largely missing.
verbatim_quote: Another important concept is seki, a situation in which neither player can play on a particular point without then allowing the other player to play at another point to capture.
